newsitem.title: USA: Amoco says Colordo Indian case not over.
newsitem.headline: Amoco says Colordo Indian case not over.

text.p: Amoco Corp said on Friday it will seek review of a federal appeals court decision that would transfer ownership of coalbed methane natural gas in Colorado to the Southern Ute Indian tribe.
However, a spokeswoman said Amoco attorneys will be studying the matter and the company has not yet decided if it will ask the U.S. Supreme Court to review the case.

On Wednesday, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 10th District said the tribe and not 2,000 other landowners who had signed leases with Amoco and other oil companies owned the coalbed methane gas worth hundreds of millions of dollars.

Amoco's Amoco Production Co holds about 70 percent of the leases, an attorney for the tribe said. Other oil companies who also had signed leases with landowners include Phillips Petroleum Co and Mobil Corp.

In a statement, Amoco said the appeals court decision could have an impact on the ownership of 20 million acres of land owned by others in several western U.S. states as it raises question about coalbed methane ownership in the deeds or patents issued by the U.S. government.

The natural gas is trapped in coal on land once part of the tribe's reservation. But the land had fallen into the hands of scores of private owners who later signed leases with Amoco and the other oil companies to develop the gas.
The tribe argued, and the appeals court agreed, that it had never conveyed ownership of the coal from which the gas is extracted.
